primary_source.title: Lectures on the Ising and Potts models on the hypercubic lattice
primary_source.author: Hugo Duminil-Copin
primary_source.source_quote: If g(β) tends to 0 as β ↗ βc, the field is said to be trivial. Otherwise, it is said to be non-trivial.
primary_source.formula: g_d(beta) = sum_{x2,x3,x4 in Z^d} U4(0,x2,x3,x4) / [chi(beta)^2 xi(beta)^d], chi = sum_x <sigma_0 sigma_x>, xi = (-lim_{n->infinity} n^(-1) log <sigma_0 sigma_{n e1}>)^(-1)
primary_source.operational_three_dimensional_statement: For the nearest-neighbor, zero-field ferromagnetic Ising model on Z^3, show that g_3(beta) does not converge to zero as beta increases to beta_c from below.
primary_source.quantifier_note: Since the ferromagnetic four-point Ursell function is nonpositive, this is equivalent to existence of epsilon>0 and beta_n increasing to beta_c with -g_3(beta_n)>=epsilon. A positive full liminf is a stronger statement. The source's prose about a non-Gaussian spin-field scaling limit is not by itself a construction or uniqueness theorem for that limit.
